messages:
Maya (support): Heads-up — BrightHealth reported a p99 jump to ~1.2s for text-generation and overall throughput down ~40% starting ~03:10 UTC. Ticket BH-487. Attaching request IDs and a small sample of traces. Anyone on runtime can take a quick look?

Ava (eng-runtime): Thanks Maya. Which model/route and region? Any recent deploys or config changes for that customer?

Maya (support): model: redwood-1.3-fp16-q4_0 (hosted). route: /api/v1/generate, region: us-east-1. Customer says it started right after a config push at 03:05. Sample request IDs: r-3a7f2, r-3a7f8. SLO is 200ms p99 historically.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot rolled out runtime v2.14.0 to us-east-1 at 03:05:12 UTC (change: kernel-selection tweaks + kv cache refactor).

Jules (perf): Noted. Can someone paste p50/p95/p99 histograms (last 1h) and a couple of representative logs? Meanwhile I'll run a quick microbench on redwood-1.3 with our smoke harness. Use: 
```
./scripts/bench/latency.py --model redwood-1.3 --seq 512 --batch 1 --warm 50 --iters 500
```
I'll run against a node in us-east-1.

Ben (oncall-infra): Checking infra metrics now. No autoscaler activities around 03:05-03:20. GPU util jumped to ~98% then throughput collapsed. PCIe error counters show a small bump on host-gpu-12. Also seeing a handful of "kv_cache_eviction" WARNs in runtime logs around 03:07.

Ava (eng-runtime): kv_cache_eviction WARNs could explain perf cliffs if customers have longer contexts and we're evicting aggressively after the refactor. Jules, can you profile with cache disabled vs enabled? Also check for increased kernel launch stalls (cuLaunch).

Ravi (eng-oncall): I'll try to repro on staging. Maya — can you share two full request traces (headers + token lengths + timestamps)?

Maya (support): Pushed traces for r-3a7f2 and r-3a7f8 to the ticket. r-3a7f2: 2.4k tokens total (long multi-turn). r-3a7f8: 900 tokens.

Jules (perf): Quick update: ran the bench. Baseline local (pre-2.14.0) p99 ~180ms. Current runtime on a canary node shows p99 ~1.1s for seq=512. Perf flamegraph points to repeated short stalls at kernel-launch path (~15-25ms per token) and hotspots around the KV cache rehydration code.

Ben (oncall-infra): Host-level differences: driver on some nodes is 535.54, others 535.63 (we rolled drivers yesterday but only partially). Also one node (host-gpu-12) shows corrected power-limit transitions — possible thermal throttling earlier today.

Ava (eng-runtime): Two actionable leads: (1) kv cache refactor + eviction policy in 2.14.0 looks suspect for long-contexts, (2) inconsistent driver versions + a marginal host could exacerbate kernel latency. For immediate mitigation, let's: 
- Shift BrightHealth traffic to the fallback variant (redwood-1.2-compat) or to dedicated pool in us-west-2.
- Revert the kv_cache refactor in 2.14.1 rollback if we confirm repro.

Ravi (eng-oncall): I'll stage a traffic switch for BrightHealth to fallback model in us-west-2 and watch p99. Will coordinate with support for routing keys.

Maya (support): Doing the customer coordination. Will message BrightHealth about temporary routing to reduce impact.

Jules (perf): On deeper profiling: the runtime shows extra memcpys between host and device during cache misses — looks like we added a memcpy on miss path in the refactor. That adds ~10-20ms per token when long sequences rehydrate KV repeatedly.

Ben (oncall-infra): Rolling driver update to 535.63 across the fleet now (will take ~12m). Also isolating host-gpu-12 for further checks. If the driver mismatch was a multiplier, this should help.

Ava (eng-runtime): Good. Two parallel efforts: Ben, finish drivers + isolate bad host. Jules, prepare a minimal patch to short-circuit the memcpy on kv miss (or revert) and post a canary build. Ravi, perform the traffic migration and capture metrics for 30m. Maya, keep BH updated. If p99 drops back under 250ms, we'll keep routed traffic; otherwise rollback runtime to 2.13.9 and open incident.

Jules (perf): I have a canary build with kv miss short-circuit. Deploying to one canary node in us-east-1 now.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot started canary of runtime v2.14.1-canary (kv short-circuit) on node canary-08 at 03:46:12 UTC.

Ravi (eng-oncall): Traffic switched at 03:50 UTC to fallback for BrightHealth. Initial p99 showing ~320ms — improvement but still above historical. Monitoring.

Ben (oncall-infra): Driver rollout complete at 03:58 UTC. Removed host-gpu-12 from rotation.

Jules (perf): Canary v2.14.1 shows p99 ~210ms on canary-08 for the same workload. Looks promising. Need to test more nodes.

Maya (support): Customer sees latency drop to ~350ms after routing; they can tolerate temporary degradation. I've opened an incident INC-2026-89 and put this thread link there.

Ava (eng-runtime): Thanks team. Plan: keep drivers rolled, monitor for 2h, promote kv short-circuit to a wider canary if stable, then decide between revert vs patch. If anything regresses, revert runtime rollout to 2.13.9 and we'll schedule a postmortem.

Maya (support): Noted. I'll update BH and the ticket.

Ben (oncall-infra): :thumbsup:

Jules (perf): Will post the profiling artifacts and a short PR with the fix for review in ~45m.

Ravi (eng-oncall): I'll keep observing traces and upload any anomalies to the incident.

Ava (eng-runtime): Great. Thanks all.
